steps.title: Pinot Noir
steps.body: Patagonia is Argentina's best region for Pinot Noir. Its cool climate and long, sunny days give red cherry, raspberry and spice, with fresh acidity and fine tannins. Old Pinot Noir vines in Río Negro, like those at Bodega Chacra, planted in 1932 and 1955, make some of South America's most acclaimed Pinots.

steps.title: Malbec and others
steps.body: Patagonian Malbec is fresher and more elegant than Mendoza's, with red fruit, violet and brighter acidity. Merlot, Cabernet Franc and Sauvignon Blanc also do well. Old Sémillon in Río Negro gives textured whites. Chubut, further south, grows Chardonnay and Pinot Noir for sparkling and still wines.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its Patagonian style.
steps.explanation: Patagonia's grapes are fresher than in the north.

steps.body: Try a Patagonian Malbec next to a Mendoza one. The southern wine is usually lighter, fresher and redder in fruit.

steps.prompt: Which grape makes some of South America's most acclaimed wines in Río Negro?
steps.explanation: Old-vine Pinot Noir, like Bodega Chacra's.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Patagonia is Argentina's best Pinot Noir region
Its Malbec is fresher and more elegant
Old Sémillon and Chubut Chardonnay add variety
